quick: 25 mg every 4 to 6 hours in combinations (historic maximum 75 mg twice daily as sustained release)
summary: Phenylpropanolamine is an alpha-adrenergic decongestant found in Indian cold combinations. The US FDA removed it from the market in 2000 after it was linked to haemorrhagic stroke, especially in young women. Its Indian regulatory status has changed over time; check the current CDSCO position before prescribing.
indications: Symptomatic relief of nasal congestion in common cold (in combination products)

dosage.d: 25 mg every 4 to 6 hours in combinations (historic maximum 75 mg twice daily as sustained release)

admin: Use only as the finished product directs
moa: Indirect and direct alpha-adrenergic agonist causing nasal vasoconstriction; also raises blood pressure.

absolute: History of stroke or intracranial haemorrhage

major: Other sympathomimetics (pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine, caffeine in high dose): additive pressor effect

emergency: Sudden severe headache or neurological deficit: emergency evaluation

counsel: Use exactly as the pack directs
Stop and seek care for rash, swelling or breathing difficulty
pearls: Prefer saline, topical decongestants for a few days, or oral antihistamine-free regimens; PPA adds stroke risk for little benefit
missed: Take it when remembered unless the next dose is due; do not double up.
overdose: Hypertension, arrhythmia, seizures: supportive care, short-acting antihypertensives (e.g. phentolamine) for crisis.
